prerequisites: No mandatory prerequisites are established. However, it is recommended that students possess basic knowledge of Chemistry and Mathematics acquired during High School or equivalent studies, especially concerning chemical formulation and nomenclature, atomic structure, chemical bonding, stoichiometry, and basic algebraic operations.

learning_outcomes.text: Reads and coherently interprets chemical terminology applied to engineering.
Formulates and solves questions and problems using appropriate chemical terminology.
Understands the different types of chemical bonds, their characteristics, and properties of materials containing them.
Understands the fundamentals of electrochemistry, corrosion, and their environmental implications.
Identifies the variables involved in a chemical reaction.
Establishes mathematical relationships involved in a chemical system.
Interprets and critiques solutions obtained in applied problems.
Organizes and participates in work teams, fostering empathy, negotiation, and optimization of time and personnel.
Behaves appropriately in the work environment, respecting the course schedule, timings, and turns to speak of the teacher and peers, and maintains an active attitude in different activities.
Provides own and novel solutions that have not been explicitly worked on in theoretical-practical sessions, analyzing the impact of these solutions on society and the environment.

syllabus_topics: UNIT 1 - Introduction to Chemistry. General Concepts.

assessment_methods.method: Written tests (objective tests, development tests, short answer tests, concept maps, etc.)
Academic work (deliverables like exercises, concept maps)

assessment_rules: The course can be passed through continuous assessment, requiring a minimum grade of 5. The continuous assessment grade is calculated as 0.6*I1 + 0.10*I2 + 0.25*I3 + 0.05*I4. For components I1 (written tests) and I2 (academic work), a minimum average grade of 3.5 is required; failing this minimum means the student must take a final exam. Students who do not participate in continuous assessment or do not pass it may take a final exam covering the entire course. If a student does not achieve a grade of 5 in the first call, they may take a final exam in the second call, where they can improve the I1 component while retaining the grades for other assessment components.
